en: The Sūtra of the Eight Great Maṇḍalas of the Mahāyāna Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Dispersing Grandee, Acting Director of the Imperial Department of Ceremonial,
and Great Master of Enlightened Teaching, Subject Fa-xian, by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying on Mount Potalaka, in the palace of the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
surrounded by hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas who paid him reverent homage.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva in the assembly named Ratnagarbha-candraprabha.
He rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, and joined his palms toward the Buddha.
He addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, I now have a question;
I pray that the Buddha, out of compassion, will sever my doubts.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnagarbha-candraprabha, saying:
"You have now asked me about the Dharma that I delight in hearing.
What is the meaning of this? I shall explain it for you.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ratnagarbha-candraprabha—
Having heard the Buddha’s words, they addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, if there are sons or daughters of good family who wish to construct the eight great maṇḍalas..."
"How should one receive, uphold, revere, and make offerings [to it]?
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent!
If there are good sons or good daughters,"
If one receives, maintains, reveres, and makes offerings to these eight great maṇḍalas according to the Dharma,
there will be great merit, and the arising of wisdom and immeasurable benefit.
"Even unto all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time,
may they all attain the accomplishment of incomparable, perfect wisdom.
Good son, listen now attentively."
I shall now explain these eight great maṇḍalas,
which possess the root heart-mantras of the eight great bodhisattvas;
if one constantly recites them and reverently makes offerings, [the benefits will be attained].
All the grave offenses of the five heinous crimes and all manner of evils shall be entirely extinguished,
and one will be able to accomplish the unsurpassed ultimate truth.
The Great Mantra is:
Oṃ mahā-vīra svāhā. This is the heart-mantra of the Buddha;
it is to be placed at the center of the maṇḍala.
Recite this great vidyā-mantra to offer worship to the Buddha.
Furthermore, the heart-vidyā-mantra of the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara is:
Oṃ hrīḥ padmaśrīye svāhā. The heart-vidyā-mantra of the Bodhisattva Maitreya is: [Oṃ maitreya svāhā].
Mehāraṇi svāhā. This is the heart-mantra of Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva.
Āgryāya svāhā. This is the heart-mantra of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
*Sahṛjja svāhā.* This is the heart-mantra of Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva.
*Kuvira svāhā.* This is the heart-mantra of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
Śrī-araṇaka svāhā. This is the heart-mantra of the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin.
Niḥsaraṇa svāhā. This is the heart-mantra of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.
Cihna-rasva-ha. Thus are the root-heart great mantras of the eight great bodhisattvas.
One should construct the Tathāgata maṇḍala.
If there are sons or daughters of good family who,
according to the ritual, receive and uphold this maṇḍala,
and with a sincere mind recite the root vidyā-mantra;
That person will swiftly attain the realization of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
This is the Buddha’s teaching of the Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Eight Great Maṇḍalas.
